rationale:
The tenth handler in this lane's bugs_open/334 scope, found by the staged-component-build lane's wire (migration 537) refusing on its first dry run — its guard tests a THIRD, better question ("can this handler's OWN orchestration_states tree ever carry a commit_sha", over a 30-day window) that neither this lane's structural census (git_commit step ∩ live handler_agent, used for 519-528/534) nor its later empirical cross-check (site_work_items.result ? commit_sha, used for 535/536) could see: the structural census DID find content-feed-orchestrator but I scoped it out deliberately at the time on volume + ambiguity grounds without deciding it; the empirical cross-check missed it because nothing has ever recorded a commit_sha for it (it is correctly silent today, not because it cannot commit, but because nothing reads its commit yet).

This is a genuinely different shape of judgement call from the two already in this batch (523 section-editor, 527 webdesign-agent), and the difference is stated plainly rather than glossed: those two each have ONE commit that is the item's own deliverable and a SEPARATE, later call that is a downstream side-effect (a deployment trigger) — picking the item's own commit was mechanical once the two were told apart. content-feed-orchestrator has NO side-effect call: commit_news and commit_rss are both genuine, independently-conditional deliverables of the SAME item (each gated on its own feed's item_count). [MEASURED 2026-08-21, all 3 orchestrations in the 30-day window] news_commit_result is present in 3/3 runs; rss_commit_result in 1/3, and on the one run where both fire they carry two DIFFERENT real shas. There is no single-field choice that loses nothing. This migration maps commit_sha to news_commit_result (the far more frequently present deliverable) and states explicitly, in the file and here, that the rarer dual-commit case loses the RSS sha from this field (it remains reachable directly via rss_commit_result, unchanged).
submitter: staged_component_build lane — RFC_029 §10.13 step 5's real gate (bdl/commit_sha), handler standardisation, found by the wire's own guard

plan.summary: Convert content-feed-orchestrator's complete step from output_fields to result_mapping, preserving all 7 existing fields and adding commit_sha sourced from news_commit_result.response.data.commit_sha — the more frequently present of two genuinely independent, co-equal commit deliverables (news 3/3 runs, rss 1/3). The rarer dual-commit case's RSS sha is disclosed as not represented in this field, remaining reachable via rss_commit_result directly.

grounded_in: Migration 537 (build-dispatch-loop's wire), staged-component-build lane: its apply-guard (property-of-the-handler test over a 30-day orchestration_states window) refused, naming content-feed-orchestrator as a producer this lane's earlier censuses missed.

content-feed-orchestrator's live workflow, read 2026-08-21: commit_news (git_commit, output_field news_commit_result) -> render_rss_xml -> ... -> commit_rss (git_commit, output_field rss_commit_result) -> complete. check_has_news/check_has_rss each gate on their own *_render_result.item_count, independently, so either commit can be skipped without the other being affected.

All 3 orchestrations in the 30-day window, read at collected_data: run 1 news-only (sha 277f6965...), run 2 BOTH (news 08b96f49..., rss b5c1059a... — two distinct real shas), run 3 news-only (sha 1870d438...). news_commit_result present 3/3, rss_commit_result present 1/3.
Same mechanism as migration 519 (output_fields cannot rename a nested path to a top-level key; the fix is a result_mapping conversion) — established earlier this session, not re-derived.

This lane's own earlier scoping note (NOTES, ~13:5xZ entry): content-feed-orchestrator was seen in the original structural census and set aside on volume + ambiguity grounds without being decided — this migration is that deferred decision, made explicitly rather than left open.
plan.risks:
1. THE news_commit_result CHOICE IS A GENUINE, DISCLOSED INFORMATION LOSS, not a mechanical fact like most of this batch's other migrations. On the ~1/3 of runs where both feeds commit, the RSS sha is real and live but NOT represented in commit_sha. Stated in the file header and here rather than hidden. If a reviewer's read of "which commit satisfies this item" differs (e.g. RSS should win, or both should somehow be represented), that is the right kind of disagreement to raise as a REVISE, not a case of missed guardrails.

2. Very low real-world volume (3 orchestrations in 30 days) — this is a door-closing conversion for the wire's guard, not a fix for an active production issue.

3. Same standing risks as the rest of the batch (no reader depends on output_fields' mode specifically; this is one of what is now 10 real handlers, not the flip itself, which remains staged-component-build's to apply once this lands).
